title: What Maker School Systems Is
definition: Maker School Systems: schools built around making things.
description:

title: The Signature Vision: Maker School Systems
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Maker School Systems.
description:
The Signature vision of Maker School Systems does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature system hulls program, charter one: master fab labs at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale system logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate safety training systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Maker School Systems becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

title: 2030 — First system hulls networks graduate 100
definition: 2030 milestone on the Maker School Systems roadmap.
description:
First system hulls networks graduate 100,000 learners with safety training credentials employers trust.

What must be true first: the fab labs results have to replicate outside the lab, system logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and safety training operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed fab labs demonstrations, system logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting safety training uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Maker School Systems
definition: Estimates Maker School Systems readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Maker School Systems components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a system hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Maker School Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Maker School Systems operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Maker School Systems installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 94986 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where fab labs monitoring, system logistics redundancy, or safety training maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Maker School Systems Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Maker School Systems: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Maker School Systems — schools built around making things.

Phase 1 — Prove (fab labs): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (system logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (safety training): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (showcase events): system hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and schools-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
key_points: Four phases: Prove, Build, Operate, Compound.
Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
